question.problem: In a coffee shop, $30%$ of customers buy a piece of cake. What is the probability that the $5$th customer of the day is the first person buying a piece of cake? Round your answer to $3$ decimal places.
question.worked_solution:
A geometric random variable $X$ with probability of success $p$ has the following probability mass function:

$$
f(x)=(1-p)^{x-1}p
$$

Let $X$ be the number of customers that enter the coffee shop until the first one buying a piece of cake. Since the chance of a customer buying a piece of cake is $30%,$ the number of customers before the first buys a piece of cake can be modeled as a geometric random variable with a probability of success

$$
p=30%=\frac{30}{100}=0.3.
$$

So, $X∼\text{Geom}(0.3).$ In this case, $X$ has the following probability mass function:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =(1-0.3)^{x-1}(0.3) \\  & =(0.7)^{x-1}(0.3)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the probability that the $5$th customer of the day is the first buying a piece of cake is

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X=5) & =f(5) \\  & =(0.7)^{5-1}(0.3) \\  & =(0.7)^{4}(0.3) \\  & ≈0.072\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $3$ decimal places.
